stem: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform magnetic field with the same velocity, perpendicular to the field. The ratio of the radii of their paths $r_\alpha:r_p$ is
model_answer: **(C) 2 : 1** $r=mv/qB$. The alpha particle has 4 times the mass and 2 times the charge, so $r_\alpha/r_p=4/2=2$.

stem: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full-scale deflection at 1 mA. To use it as a voltmeter of range 0–10 V you must connect
model_answer: **(A) 9900 Ω in series** $R=\dfrac{V}{I_g}-G=\dfrac{10}{10^{-3}}-100=9900$ Ω, in series.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
**Assertion (A):** A charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field keeps a constant kinetic energy.
**Reason (R):** The magnetic force on a moving charge is always perpendicular to its velocity, so it does no work.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are false.
model_answer: **(A)** No work is done, so the speed and kinetic energy stay constant; only the direction changes.

stem: Two long parallel wires 10 cm apart carry currents of 5 A and 10 A in the same direction. Find the force per metre on each wire and state whether it is attractive or repulsive.
model_answer:
$\dfrac FL=\dfrac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}$ [½]

$=\boxed{1\times10^{-4}\text{ N m}^{-1}}$ [½]
Currents in the same direction: **attractive**. [½]

stem: Using the Biot–Savart law, derive an expression for the magnetic field at a point on the axis of a circular loop of radius $R$ carrying current $I$, at distance $x$ from its centre. Write the field at the centre.
model_answer:
Diagram: loop, element $d\vec l$, point P on the axis, $r=\sqrt{R^2+x^2}$; $d\vec l\perp\hat r$. [½]
Biot–Savart: $dB=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I\,dl}{R^2+x^2}$ [½]
Components perpendicular to the axis cancel in pairs; axial components $dB\sin\phi$ add, with $\sin\phi=\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+x^2}}$. [1]
$B=\dfrac{\mu_0IR}{4\pi(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}}\oint dl=\boxed{\dfrac{\mu_0IR^2}{2(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}}}$ along the axis; at the centre $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2R}$. [1]

label: PYQ-style
stem: A rectangular coil of 50 turns, 4 cm × 5 cm, carries 2 A in a uniform field of 0.2 T. Find (i) its magnetic moment, (ii) the maximum torque on it, (iii) the torque when its normal makes $30^\circ$ with the field.
model_answer:
(i) $m=NIA=50\times2\times(0.04\times0.05)=\boxed{0.2\text{ A m}^2}$ [1]
(ii) $\tau_\text{max}=mB=0.2\times0.2=\boxed{0.04\text{ N m}}$ (normal perpendicular to B) [1]
(iii) $\tau=mB\sin30^\circ=0.04\times\tfrac12=\boxed{0.02\text{ N m}}$ [1]
hint: $\tau=NIAB\sin\theta$ with θ between B and the normal.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Explain the principle and working of a moving coil galvanometer with a labelled diagram. Why is a radial field used? Obtain an expression for its current sensitivity. [3]
(b) A galvanometer of resistance 20 Ω gives full-scale deflection at 5 mA. How can it be converted into an ammeter of range 0–5 A? [2]
model_answer:
(a) Labelled diagram: coil on a soft-iron core between concave pole pieces, spring/suspension, pointer. [1]
Principle: a current loop in a magnetic field feels a torque. Concave poles and the core make the field radial, so the coil's plane is always along B and the deflecting torque is $NIAB$ at every angle. Equilibrium: $NIAB=k\phi$. [1]
$\phi=\dfrac{NAB}{k}I$, so current sensitivity $\boxed{\dfrac{\phi}{I}=\dfrac{NAB}{k}}$ [1]
(b) Shunt $S=\dfrac{I_gG}{I-I_g}=\dfrac{5\times10^{-3}\times20}{5-0.005}$ [1]
$\approx\boxed{0.02\ \Omega}$, connected **in parallel** with the galvanometer. [1]
